title: Europe · breeds of the continent
blurb: Britain, Germany, Switzerland and the Low Countries: the herders, guards and terriers that became the world's most widely kept dogs.

items.d: The sheepdog of the Anglo-Scottish border: black and white, tireless, and the standard for herding trials.
The German service breed: herder, police dog and guide dog, 55–65 cm of steady nerve.
German butcher's drover and guard dog: stocky, confident and protective of its people.
Created in Thuringia in the 1890s as a guard and companion: lean, alert and quick to learn.
Alpine rescue dog of the hospice pass: 64–120 kg, with a famous nose for snowbound travellers.
English flushing spaniel that springs game from cover; 19–25 kg, busy and biddable.
Small English working terrier, 25–30 cm, bred to bolt foxes and follow a scent underground.
White Scottish terrier from Argyll, bred for otter and fox and kept for its cheerful temper.
